data.title: Energean profit jumps 54% on higher oil prices as Katlan project stays on track
data.description:
The Israel-based Eastern Mediterranean gas producer said net profit for the nine months to Sept. 30 rose to $317m from $206m a year earlier. The increase was driven by a 44% rise in realised liquids prices to $88 a barrel, reflecting stronger oil market conditions during the period.

Operational performance remained solid, with average production of 139,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (kboed), in line with the company's guidance. Adjusted EBITDAX rose 7% to $888m, while production costs excluding royalties fell 10% to $193m, supporting profitability.

Energean maintained its production outlook for the full year of 130-140 kboed and said the Katlan offshore gas development in Israel remains on track to deliver first gas in the first half of 2027. Total development expenditure for the project is expected to be around $1.25bn, with the company having secured a $700m 10-year loan to support financing.

The London-listed group also reaffirmed its commitment to shareholder returns, declaring a third-quarter dividend of $0.10 per share and saying it expects to return about $110m to shareholders in 2026.

Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com

data.title: Swiss Trade Surplus Grows In October
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Switzerland's foreign trade surplus increased in October as exports grew faster than imports, data from the Federal Customs Administration showed on Thursday.

The trade surplus climbed to CHF 3.2 billion in October from CHF 1.2 billion in September.

In real terms, exports climbed 2.4 percent monthly in October, and imports were 0.7 percent higher.

Exports of chemicals and pharmaceutical products-key sectors for Switzerland's economy-grew 11.2 percent in October. Watch exports, another major Swiss industry, rose 4.6 percent. On the import side, Switzerland brought in 18.5 percent fewer jewelry items.

Separate official data from the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry showed that watch exports rose 9.1 percent annually in October, driven largely by increased demand for steel and bimetallic watches.

data.title: Bitcoin, Ether Recover as Traders Digest Fed Rate-Hike Signals
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin and ether rebounded Thursday after slipping earlier following the release of the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, which came out hawkish.

Bitcoin was 1.9% higher at $63,442 after tumbling as low as $62,086 in the previous session, while ether rose 2.2% to $1,801.50. The minutes showed that almost all Fed officials supported further rate hikes, with a handful considering an increase of half a percentage point in December.

Rate hikes increase the opportunity cost of holding nonyielding assets, including cryptocurrencies, as bonds become relatively more attractive. Traders are pricing a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike in December, with a 10% chance of a half-point rise, according to CME FedWatch.

Crypto investors now turn to Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering, with the company's shares expected to list Thursday. Some market participants attributed bitcoin's latest slide to investors channeling funds out of crypto assets and into the Claude developer's flotation.

"Given the investment profile, this type of allocation usually falls in the same bucket as bitcoin, and it would be consistent with investors selling bitcoin into weakness to make room," said Mauricio Di Bartolomeo, co-founder of bitcoin lending platform Ledn.

Write to Joseph Wilkins at joseph.wilkins@wsj.com

data.title: Johnson Matthey H1 Pre-Tax Profit Falls; Raises FY Underlying Operating Profit Outlook; Ups Dividend
data.description:
LONDON (dpa-AFX) - Johnson Matthey Plc (JMAT.L), a speciality chemicals and sustainable technologies company, Thursday reported lower pre-tax profit from continuing operations for the first half, despite higher revenue, mainly due to impairment charges on investments in associates and financial assets. The company also raised its full-year outlook for underlying operating profit.

Profit before tax from continuing operations declined to £15 million from £86 million a year ago.

The company recorded impairment charges of £63 million on investments in associates and £62 million on financial assets, compared with no such charges in the prior-year period.

Excluding one-time items, underlying pre-tax profit rose 47% to £162 million from £110 million last year.

Net loss from continuing operations was £15 million or 11.8p per share, compared with £16 million or 12.7p per share loss a year ago.

Underlying profit from continuing operations increased to £129 million or 102.2p per basic share from £86 million or 68.2p per basic share last year.

Including discontinued operations, the company reported net profit of £335 million or 262.5 pence per share, compared with a loss of £18 million or 14.2 pence per share a year ago.

Operating profit rose to £170 million from £117 million last year, while underlying operating profit climbed 32% to £187 million.

Revenue increased 35% to £7.206 billion from £5.353 billion in the previous year.

The Board approved an interim dividend of 22.7p per share, up 3% from 22p per share a year ago, payable on February 2, to shareholders on record as of November 27.

For the full year, the company now expects group underlying operating profit to grow at a high single-digit percentage rate, compared with its previous outlook for low- to mid-single-digit growth, at constant precious metal prices and constant currency.

On the LSE, Johnson Matthey shares closed down 1.28% at 2,320p on Wednesday.

data.title: UK's Royal Mail taps finance chief Ablin as CEO amid calls for parcel market reforms
data.description:
Royal Mail owner International Distribution Services (IDS) named finance chief Paul Ablin as the British postal group's new CEO on Thursday, while renewing its warning that the firm is competing on an "unlevel playing field" against rivals in the parcels market.

Royal Mail's current CEO Alistair Cochrane will retire at the end of 2026, with Ablin taking over from January 2027.

The more than 500-year-old company, whose iconic red post boxes with the Royal Crest dot Britain, has been repeatedly probed and fined over missed delivery targets by UK regulators, as it also struggles with falling letter volumes.

In October, Royal Mail implemented a Universal Service reform to address the issues and announced plans to cut up to 2,500 jobs by the end of 2027.

"We welcome the Government’s plans to tackle bogus self-employment and will continue to push for strong and enforceable standards across the industry," IDS chief Martin Seidenberg said in a statement.

Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle said the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms that did not employ staff under the same conditions and urged the British government to act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail, a BBC report said on Tuesday.

Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky's EP Group closed its acquisition of IDS in June 2025 after committing to protect Royal Mail and its workers and customers.

IDS forecast that Royal Mail’s second-half performance will be hurt by the delay to some mail price increases that were due to take effect last month.

While Royal Mail revenue rose 3.9% to £4.13 billion ($5.42 billion) in the six months to September 27 and parcel volumes grew 8%, addressed letter volumes were down 8% in the period.

data.title: Gigasun signs a new order in China worth approximately 67 MSEK
data.description:
Gigasun's wholly owned subsidiary in China has signed a new agreement with a logistics company. The agreement concerns the installation of a solar power plant with a total capacity of approximately 6.8 megawatts (MW) in Guangdong Province.

The facility is expected to generate annual revenues of approximately 3.4 MSEK from electricity sales. This corresponds to a total order value of approximately 68 MSEK over the 20-year term of the agreement.

The investment in the facility amounts to approximately 26.4 MSEK, and the project is planned to start during the fourth quarter of 2026. The facility will be owned and operated by Gigasun's subsidiary and is expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 3,300 tons per year.

The project is fully commercially viable without the need for government subsidies.

CEO Max Metelius comments:

New projects are now being signed at a time when we have significantly reduced our financing costs, which increases the selection of profitable projects and makes every new megawatt more valuable to shareholders. We can also note that solar irradiation in October was back to normal levels after a third quarter affected by unusually low irradiation.

For more information, please contact:

Max Metelius, CEO Gigasun AB (publ)

Phone: +46 (0) 72 316 04 44

E-mail: max.metelius@gigasun.se

Stefan Salomonsson, CFO Gigasun AB (publ)

Phone: +46 (0) 70 220 80 00

E-mail: stefan.salomonsson@gigasun.se

Certified Advisor is FNCA Sweden AB

About the operation

Gigasun operates in China through its wholly owned subsidiaries Advanced Soltech Renewable Energy (Hangzhou) Co. Ltd (“ASRE”) and Longrui Solar Energy (Suqian) Co. Ltd. (“SQ”), and Suqian Ruiyan New Energy Co., Ltd. (“RY”).

The business model consists of financing, installing, owning and managing solar PV installations on customers' roofs in China. The customer does not pay for the solar PV installation, but instead enters an agreement to buy the electricity that the solar PV installation produces under a 20-year agreement. Current income comes from the sale of electricity to customers and governmental subsidies.

The goal is to have an installed capacity of 1,000 megawatts (MW) in the medium term.

data.title: Historically 'Normal' Rates Improve Fixed-Income Return Prospects — Market Talk
data.description: Rates are back to historically "normal" levels, improving fixed income's long-term return prospects, PGIM Credit's Robert Tipp says in a note. Still, yields may have not yet peaked, keeping the chief investment strategist cautious on long duration. Following the recent upward shift, it is possible that rates reached restrictive levels that could conceivably bring inflation to heel, he says. "Yet, given this cycle is host of upward drivers for growth and inflation, our suspicion is that another stair-step higher for the developed market yield curve may be required to bring inflation back down to target," Tipp says. However, it may take some time for central banks and markets to make that call, he adds. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Deutsche Telekom invests €100 million in France's Mistral AI
data.description:
Deutsche Telekom said on Thursday its investment arm had invested €100 million ($110 million) in the Series D funding round of French startup Mistral AI, laying the groundwork for a strategic partnership between the companies.

The companies said they planned to help businesses and public-sector organisations in Germany adopt AI tools tailored to their needs, particularly in industrial and regulated sectors.

The investment by Deutsche Telekom's T.Capital Tech Fund comes as European policymakers and companies seek to build domestic AI capabilities and reduce dependence on US providers like OpenAI and Anthropic .

Founded in 2023, Mistral AI develops open-weight AI models and is one of Europe's largest AI startups. The company raised €3 billion in its latest funding round, valuing it at more than €21 billion.

data.title: South African Central Bank's Restrictive Stance Could Support Rand — Market Talk
data.description: The South African rand has scope to recover, supported by its attractive yields and the central bank's restrictive policy stance, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The South African Reserve Bank is expected to leave rates unchanged in a decision at 1300 GMT after raising rates to 7.25% in September. "However, money markets do price another 25 bps hike in early 2027," Turner says. The SARB has been responsive to the inflation shock and this should benefit the rand, he says. The dollar rises 0.1% to 17.2860 rand after reaching a one-year high of 17.3602 overnight, according to LSEG, but ING expects it to fall to 16.0000 in 2H of 2027. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Indonesian Rupiah Likely to Continue to Underperform — Market Talk
data.description: The Indonesian rupiah will likely continue to underperform, says ING's Deepali Bhargava at a media roundtable. Political governance and policy stability have been pretty weak, the Asia-Pacific regional head of research adds. Government measures could still be seen as populist ahead of the country's next general election, which is a few years away, she says. "Investors are looking at the policy environment more closely and we've not seen that change in a big way," she adds. MSCI has also launched a consultation on a potential reclassification of Indonesia to standalone from emerging-market status. If the downgrade happens, it will be a big risk for investors, Bhargava says. The dollar rises 0.1% to 18,235 rupiah, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
